title: Analysis notebook — who-wins distribution, agree-vs-disagree rate, drift/nudge frequency per side, tokens/latency per round (Epic 14, issue #98)
prompt:
Create a notebook in notebooks/ analysing: who-wins distribution, agree-vs-disagree rate, drift/nudge frequency per side (evidence anti-sycophancy works), tokens/latency per round.

Follow repo standards: TDD (write the failing test first, then code); max 150 lines per code file (split, don't compress); ruff = 0 violations + mypy clean; no hard-coded values (read from config); every external API call goes through the API gatekeeper (Epic 13); log via the LOG package; keep coverage >= 85%. Read docs/PRD.md and the relevant docs/prds/*.md before starting.

usage.summary: Read PRD §9 + the 14.1 core/research package and one runs/*.jsonl end-to-end; regenerated runs/dataset/runs_summary.csv to 4 runs; TDD red-first analysis test; built a tested analysis module reused by a thin notebook; full gate suite.

note: Implements the PRD §9 results analysis as a notebook. KEY TECHNIQUE: all reusable logic lives in a TESTED module (agent_debate.core.research.analysis) and the notebook (notebooks/analysis.ipynb) is THIN — it imports the module, calls pure functions, and prints tables. This keeps the analyses under the TDD/coverage gate (notebooks can't be unit-tested cleanly) and the notebook's code cells minimal/clean. TDD RED-FIRST: packages/core/tests/test_research_analysis.py (10 tests, synthetic RunSummary rows + synthetic JSONL fixtures — never the committed runs) watched the import of the new analysis functions fail, then implemented to green. NEW packages/core/src/agent_debate/core/research/analysis.py (~199 lines incl. docstrings, 71 code lines — under the 150 cap) with five pure functions building on the 14.1 RunSummary + parsing round-level detail the summary doesn't carry: who_wins (Counter per winner, ties included), agree_vs_disagree (converged True/False counts + agree_rate, 0.0 on empty — no div-by-zero), nudges_per_side (NudgeStats: pro/con totals + per-run breakdown — the anti-sycophancy evidence), round_metrics (parses message events from one run's JSONL into per-round tokens/latency with a per-side pro/con token split — RunSummary only has run-level totals), tokens_latency_per_topic (TopicMetric per run). Wired into research/__init__.py public surface. NEW notebooks/analysis.ipynb: valid nbformat-4 JSON, 13 cells, 5 markdown sections (4 analyses + summary). The first cell resolves the runs dir from agent_debate.log.DEFAULT_RUNS_DIR anchored to the repo root (first parent holding pyproject.toml + the runs dir) so it works regardless of the kernel cwd and never picks up a stray LOG-chatter 'runs' folder that importing the package creates in cwd. Committed with CLEARED OUTPUTS (no embedded run output -> no stale numbers / no accidental secrets). NEW notebooks/README.md (how to run via `uv run --with jupyter ...`, what each analysis shows, the tables-not-charts/14.3 deps note). DEPS DECISION: matplotlib/pandas are NOT workspace deps and rich visualisation is the SEPARATE task 14.3, so 14.2 stays stdlib-only and presents tables; Jupyter is pulled in on demand via `uv run --with jupyter`, not added as a permanent dep. NEW lightweight stdlib smoke test packages/core/tests/test_analysis_notebook.py (no nbformat/nbclient dep added — those aren't workspace deps): asserts the notebook is valid nbformat-4 JSON, carries the 4 analysis sections, and ships with cleared outputs. NOTE: ruff/mypy in pyproject only scan packages/*/src + tests + select scripts, so the notebook is outside the lint/type gate (confirmed — no gate loosening needed). REGENERATED runs/dataset/runs_summary.csv via `python scripts/aggregate_runs.py` to include all 4 runs (was 3); committed the refreshed CSV. EXECUTED the notebook end-to-end (uv run --with jupyter --with nbclient jupyter nbconvert --execute) against the real runs and sanity-checked: 4 runs; who_wins = {pro:2, con:1, tie:1} (capitalism=pro, policy=pro, techethics=con, lifestyle=tie); agree_vs_disagree = 0 agree / 4 disagree (0% — adversarial format, converged mostly False as expected); nudges = 0/0 per side on every run (the staged-drift detection path is exercised by the engine tests 8.4; the real sample runs needed no nudge — noted in the notebook); per-round tokens/latency grow with round count (capitalism round 9 ~50.9k tokens / ~99s vs round 1 ~10.4k / ~22s). GATES GREEN: uv sync clean; ruff check . = All checks passed; ruff format --check . = 242 files already formatted; mypy = Success, no issues in 239 source files; pytest --cov = 841 passed, 99% total coverage (research package 94%, analysis.py 93% — both >= 85%); check_line_limit.py rc=0; secret_scan.py = only the live local .env (the documented pre-existing finding), zero hits on any committed file incl. the refreshed CSV and the cleared-output notebook. PRE-EXISTING failures unchanged (6 failed + 2 errors, identical on clean main): branch-protection Unix perms x2, live-tree secret scan/hygiene x2 (real .env), Windows missing-file path-regex x2 (test_price_table, test_rate_limit_config), long-topic parametrized teardown errors x2 — NO new failures introduced. Files: NEW core/research/analysis.py, core/tests/test_research_analysis.py, core/tests/test_analysis_notebook.py, notebooks/analysis.ipynb, notebooks/README.md, this artifact; EDIT core/research/__init__.py (export the 5 analysis fns + 3 result models), runs/dataset/runs_summary.csv (refreshed to 4 runs), docs/PROMPTS.md (14.2 entry), docs/TASKS.md (14.2 [x]). Closes #98.
